question: Does rustc codegen (opt-level, codegen-units, LTO) affect the IN-GUEST liteinst syscall-handler hot path in a way it did NOT for the ptrace supervisor?
supervisor_binary: hermit release bin, held FIXED across all runs (lifecycle-only for liteinst)
artifact_under_test: libreverie_liteinst.so, selected per-run via HERMIT_LITEINST_RUNTIME; only its codegen varies
metric: ns per in-guest getpid handler invocation = CPU-time (user+sys) SLOPE across N=1e5 and N=2e6, /(dN)*1e9; fixed startup/patch/teardown cancels in the slope; CPU-time immune to wall noise floor
box_state: single-core pinned (taskset -c 300) + boxed (systemd-run --user unit); serial; 5 measured reps/point + 1 discarded warmup; median
vacuity_guard: every timed run required direct_hook=N+1 and ptrace_installation=0 (proves in-guest path exercised, no ptrace, no silent fallback)
profile_facts: hermit workspace Cargo.toml and liteinst-runtime-build/Cargo.toml BOTH have zero [profile.*] stanzas => release inherits cargo defaults opt-level=3, codegen-units=16, lto=false. Variant A == shipping config.

matrix.D: opt-level=0 (CONTROL / discriminator: proves the metric responds to codegen)

command: systemd-run --user --unit=inguest-codegen-matrix -p (implicit) bash run-matrix.sh A:so/A.so B:so/B.so C:so/C.so D:so/D.so ; then rebuild_csv.py (parses raw /usr/bin/time -v files) ; analyze.py
note_on_csv: The live run-matrix.sh CPU extractor had a leading-TAB awk bug (all cpu=0). Raw /usr/bin/time -v files were correct; results.csv was rebuilt from them via rebuild_csv.py. The run-matrix.sh copy here retains the taskset pin; use rebuild_csv.py as the authoritative parser.
